text: The College of Nursing at Dubai Medical University proudly recognizes Dr. Abdullah Alshammari,for serving as an External Examiner for a PhD thesis defense at the University of Pécs in Hungary.

Dr. Alshammari’s selection for this distinguished academic role reflects his recognized expertise in community and mental health nursing, as well as his active contribution to doctoral education, research quality, and international academic scholarship. As an External Examiner, he provided an independent and rigorous evaluation of the doctoral research, assessed its scientific quality and contribution to knowledge, and contributed expert insights during the scholarly discussion and examination process.

The thesis, entitled “Well-being, Life Satisfaction, and Optimal Living Profile: Cross-Cultural Studies Among Hungarian and Jordanian University Students,” examined well-being and life satisfaction across different cultural contexts. The research addresses an important and timely area with significant relevance to mental health, student well-being, quality of life, and higher education.

Through his participation in the public defense, Dr. Alshammari contributed to a high-level international academic exchange and supported the advancement of cross-cultural research in health and well-being. His role also strengthened scholarly connections between Dubai Medical University and the international academic community.

The College of Nursing commends Dr. Alshammari for representing the College in this important academic capacity. His contribution demonstrates the caliber and expertise of the College’s faculty and reflects its strong commitment to research excellence, doctoral scholarship, academic quality assurance, and meaningful international collaboration.

The College also extends its sincere congratulations to Dr. Farah Ziad Khalil Abu Khadra on the successful completion of her PhD and wishes her continued success in her academic and professional journey.

DMU’s Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini Joins Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration – Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group

Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) Program, and Chair of the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee at Dubai Medical University (DMU), as a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working

Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Director of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) Program, and Chair of the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee at Dubai Medical University (DMU), as a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group under the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration (ANIC) — a milestone that strengthens the College’s growing regional footprint in interprofessional education and collaborative practice research.

ANIC — the Arab Network for Interprofessional Collaboration — is a regional body dedicated to fostering interprofessional education and collaborative practice (IPECP) across academia and healthcare systems throughout the Arab world. The Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group serves as one of ANIC’s key sub-groups, charged with identifying priority research themes, strengthening regional research capacity, and disseminating best practices to inform policy and inspire innovation at member institutions.

The Working Group operates with three core objectives: establishing a collaborative research framework tailored to the specific IPECP needs and priorities of Arab countries; building research capacity across academic and clinical institutions through mentorship, faculty development, and joint projects; and promoting the dissemination of research findings and best practices to advance interprofessional learning at a regional and international level.As a member of the Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group, Dr. El Ouweini will contribute his expertise in clinical pharmacy practice and academic program leadership to support ANIC’s regional agenda. His work within the group will focus on identifying collaborative research opportunities, connecting academic and healthcare institutions across the Arab region, and helping build a sustainable culture of interprofessional inquiry aligned with the healthcare priorities of Arab countries.

This appointment is a natural extension of Dr. El Ouweini’s ongoing work at DMU, where he chairs the DMU’s Interprofessional Education Committee through its longitudinal IPE program developed in partnership with the DMU College of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing. His involvement at the ANIC level will further position DMU as a key contributor to regional IPECP dialogue and research.

The ANIC Research Collaboration & Impact Working Group has set an ambitious roadmap that includes establishing formal inter-institutional partnerships, publishing collaborative peer-reviewed research, building a regional database of IPECP collaborators, and hosting capacity-building workshops and webinars for faculty and researchers across the Arab world. The group also envisions a biannual ANIC conference and an annual IPECP newsletter as key vehicles for regional knowledge sharing.

On 23 May 2026, the College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) made a strong and impactful showing at MedEngineers 2026, a landmark healthcare innovation festival hosted by MedHack Global at the American University of Sharjah. The event brought together students, healthcare professionals, engineers, innovators, and members of the public from across the UAE, creating a vibrant platform for collaboration, creativity, and the future of healthcare. DMU was represented by three active pharmacy student clubs — the DMU-IVPN Student Club, the UAE Pharmacy Students Federation – DMU chapter (UPSF-DMU), and the Integrative Medicine Society (IMS) — alongside students who competed in the event’s flagship Hackathon competition.

MedEngineers 2026 was designed to bridge the healthcare and engineering disciplines, bringing university clubs and student societies together from institutions across the UAE to set up interactive booths, exchange ideas, and showcase student-led projects. The festival simultaneously hosted a competitive Hackathon where multidisciplinary teams of medical and engineering students worked together to design innovative solutions to real-world healthcare challenges.

The event drew participation from a diverse range of universities, including Gulf Medical University (GMU), UAE University (UAEU), Ajman University (AU), and many others, creating rich networking opportunities and meaningful dialogue about the future of healthcare across disciplines and institutions.

The DMU-IVPN Student Club, supervised by Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, represented DMU with an engaging and interactive booth, introducing visitors to the goals and initiatives of the club as well as those of the Global IVPN Network, which aims to empower healthcare professionals worldwide. The booth featured several hands-on activities designed to stimulate thinking around clinical pharmacy and healthcare technology.

In the popular “Guess the Drug” activity, participants were challenged to identify commonly used medications based on clinical scenarios. The “You Are the Pharmacist” activity invited visitors to step into a pharmacist’s role and make quick clinical decisions based on patient-specific situations. A third activity invited participants to identify healthcare technologies from provided clues — offering valuable insight into the critical importance of informatics and digital tools in modern healthcare delivery.

The Integrative Medicine Society (IMS), supervised by Dr. Naglaa Saad and Eng. Hessa Lootah, captivated visitors with a booth that elegantly blended traditional healing with modern innovation. Attendees were introduced to natural therapeutic approaches and traditional healing practices through interactive activities including a “Myth or Fact” game about medicinal herbs and a “Smell and Guess” challenge. Visitors also had the unique opportunity to create personalized herbal tea blends using peppermint, chamomile, and lavender.

A standout highlight at the IMS booth was Layla, the society’s AI-powered Integrative Medicine Assistant, which answered visitors’ questions in real time and demonstrated how technology can be harnessed to advance health education. The booth also showcased three exciting student-developed projects — EaseHer, NeuroBoost, and AyurJelly — exemplifying the creativity and entrepreneurial spirit of DMU students.

The UAE Pharmacy Students Federation – DMU Chapter (UPSF-DMU), supervised by Dr. Yasmein Yasser, also set up a vibrant interactive booth at MedEngineers 2026, engaging visitors through crossword puzzles, medication-matching exercises, clinical case scenarios, and quiz-style questions. Medical-themed prizes and rewards kept the atmosphere lively and educational, drawing visitors of all ages — from school students and parents to practicing healthcare professionals.

Through these interactions, UPSF-DMU representatives had the opportunity to discuss DMU’s programs, career pathways in pharmacy, and the value of student involvement in professional and community activities — helping to raise the profile of the pharmacy profession among a broad public audience.

Among the highlights of DMU’s participation was the outstanding performance of pharmacy student Nabiha Sadick Batcha in the MedEngineers Hackathon. Competing as part of a multidisciplinary team, Nabiha collaborated with her colleagues Nimrah Ahmer Afaq and Shams Haider from DMU’s College of Medicine, alongside Aysha Naaman AlKaabi, an engineering student from UAE University (UAEU).

Their innovative project, Smart Heal Cast, earned the team second place in the Hackathon competition. The ten finalist teams pitched their ideas to a panel of judges, with audience votes also factored into the final results. The collaborative achievement stands as a testament to the power of interdisciplinary teamwork — uniting pharmacy, medicine, and engineering expertise to address real healthcare challenges.

Dubai Medical University College of Pharmacy Makes History with First APhA Immunization Certification Program in the UAE

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) has marked an important milestone in pharmacy education in the United Arab Emirates by successfully organizing and delivering the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery Certificate Program — the first time this internationally accredited program has been offered by a UAE College of Pharmacy. Led

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University (DMU) has marked an important milestone in pharmacy education in the United Arab Emirates by successfully organizing and delivering the American Pharmacists Association (APhA) Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery Certificate Program — the first time this internationally accredited program has been offered by a UAE College of Pharmacy.

Led by Dr. Sahar Al-Najjar and supported by dedicated faculty members of the DMU College of Pharmacy, this pioneering program marks a transformative step in preparing the next generation of pharmacists in the UAE to serve as certified immunizers.

The APhA Immunization Delivery Certificate Program is a rigorous, multi-component curriculum recognized across the globe for its high standards in immunization training. The DMU-hosted program was structured as follows:

Participants completed two weeks of asynchronous, self-paced online coursework delivered directly through the APhA platform. Modules covered the immunological foundations of vaccines, the immunization schedule, vaccine storage and handling, patient screening and assessment, documentation and reporting requirements, and the management of adverse events.
Self-Paced Online Theory Modules (Two Weeks):

Following successful completion of the online modules, students attended an intensive, hands-on practical training day hosted at DMU Hospital (DMUH). Under the direct supervision of qualified faculty, participants developed and refined the clinical techniques required for safe and effective vaccine administration, including injection technique, patient communication, and emergency response protocols.
Full-Day Practical Skills Training:

The program concluded with a comprehensive assessment comprising both a written theory examination on the APhA module content and a practical skills evaluation. Students who successfully met all requirements were formally awarded the APhA Pharmacy-Based Immunization Delivery certificate, recognizing them as certified immunizers.
Comprehensive Certification Examination:

The program was delivered to second-year students of the Master of Clinical Pharmacy (M.Pharm) program at DMU, who are currently engaged in their advanced clinical rotations. These students represent the forefront of clinical pharmacy practice in the UAE, and their certification as immunizers further equips them to contribute meaningfully to patient care and public health upon entering professional practice.

This achievement is particularly significant given the evolving regulatory landscape in the UAE. Legislation that enables pharmacist-administered immunizations is already in place, and the DMU College of Pharmacy has proactively ensured that its graduates are not only knowledgeable but formally certified and practice-ready from day one. By completing this program, the M.Pharm graduates are positioned to seamlessly assume the role of immunizers as soon as the regulatory framework is implemented across healthcare settings.

The College of Nursing at Dubai Medical University proudly celebrated International Nurses Day on 14 May 2026, recognizing the dedication, compassion, leadership, and indispensable contributions of nurses to healthcare and society.

The celebration was held under the leadership of Prof. Maxime Merheb, Dean of the College of Health Sciences and Acting Dean of the College of Nursing, who reaffirmed the College’s commitment to preparing highly competent, compassionate, and future-ready nursing professionals. In his address, Prof. Merheb highlighted the essential role of nurses as frontline healthcare leaders and emphasized the importance of excellence in nursing education, clinical competence, professional ethics, and service to the community.

The event brought together faculty and staff members from the College of Nursing, as well as colleagues from the College of Medicine and the College of Pharmacy. Their participation reflected Dubai Medical University’s strong culture of interdisciplinary collaboration and its shared commitment to advancing healthcare education and strengthening the healthcare workforce.

A key highlight of the celebration was the active participation of first- and second-year nursing students, who demonstrated their creativity, knowledge, and pride in the profession. The students produced an inspiring video highlighting the vital role of nurses and their unwavering commitment to patient care. the webinar addressed the complex clinical considerations involved in optimizing pharmacotherapy for patients who fast given the significant physiological, dietary, sleep, and hydration changes that occur during Ramadan. Spontaneous Congenital Transmesenteric Internal Hernia in an Adult Without Prior Abdominal Surgery: A Rare Cause of Acute Small Bowel Obstruction by Sana Ahmed, Laian Mohamad Hamod,Leen Ibrahim Sabbagh,Rokia Malahifci, Maryam Munzer Manzalgi.
